messages:
Nina (partnerships): Heads up — prepping partner-facing playbook for the edge runtime shim we promised to Marketplace vendors. Want to align on compatibility guarantees, deprecation windows, and what we tell SI partners. Thinking: 6mo notice for breaking changes + a fallback shim we support for one release. Thoughts?
Kai (eng-runtime): +1 on 6mo, but need to scope what "fallback shim" covers. For edge builds we can supply a binary adapter for x86 and a trimmed shim for arm64. It won't cover custom quantization or private ops.
Alex (partner-eng): Important to call out Marketplace validation gates. Some vendors require signed binaries and specific CI artifacts. If we expect partners to consume the shim, we should provide signed releases and a reproducible build artifact.
Nina (partnerships): Good call on signed artifacts. Also we should prescribe the communication cadence: announce earliest, then partner-only beta, then public deprecation notice at 3mo, then final removal at 6mo. Does that map to support SLAs?
Sam (legal): Need to ensure the playbook language doesn't create forced-support obligations beyond our SOW. Suggest: "grace period" and "best-effort compatibility" phrasing for third-party vendor integrations. Also include export-control checklist for on-prem customers.
Daniel (product): From product POV we need rollout canaries: 1) internal canary on Dedicated, 2) partner canary (opt-in), 3) 50% Marketplace traffic, then full. That sequence gives us telemetry to validate. Add a rollback plan with automatic fallback to the hosted variant if latency/regressions exceed thresholds.
Kai (eng-runtime): Telemetry gating: recommend we fail early if token-latency P95 increases >30% or error rate >0.5% for 10 minutes. We can wire an automated circuit to redirect partner calls to the hosted model variant.
Alex (partner-eng): For partner onboarding doc, include a short compatibility checklist: supported OS/arch, minimum runtime version, required env vars, expected model formats, how to enable shim via feature flag, and a sample canary YAML. Keep it copy-paste friendly.
Nina (partnerships): I'll draft the comms timeline and partner email templates. Alex — can you sketch the partner checklist? Kai — can you and eng-runtime own the gating metrics and rollback hooks? Sam — can you review the legal phrasing?
Alex (partner-eng): Yep, I'll put a first-pass checklist in the doc by EOD tomorrow.
Kai (eng-runtime): I'll add the telemetry thresholds and a sample circuit-breaker config. Also proposing a small test harness we can hand to partners to validate shim behavior on their infra.
Sam (legal): I'll review the draft and send redlines by Thursday. One ask: include a template addendum for Enterprise contracts that opt into extended backcompat support for a fee.
Daniel (product): We should also loop in marketplace ops on the signed artifact requirements — they manage the ingestion pipeline. I'll ping them after we have the draft.
deploy-bot: deploy #edge-shim-prototype succeeded to staging — build 2026.03.22-87a1.
Nina (partnerships): Nice — Kai, once the staging build is stable, let's schedule a 30m partner sync next week with 2-3 vendor reps. Agenda: overview, checklist walk-through, signing/provenance, and canary timetable.
Kai (eng-runtime): Sounds good. Also: any thought about SDK surface-level shims vs binary shims? I prefer binary (less churn) but SDK shims give partners faster integration for Python/JS.
Alex (partner-eng): Offer both but make SDK shims explicitly unsupported for custom runtime patches. Recommend binary shim as primary, SDK shim as transitional. Document maintenance windows for both.
Nina (partnerships): Decision noted: binary primary, SDK transitional. Action items: Nina — comms + sync invite; Alex — partner checklist; Kai — telemetry/gate + test harness; Sam — legal review; Daniel — marketplace ops intro. I'll follow up with a shared doc link in this thread. :thumbsup:
Kai (eng-runtime): Quick Q: do we version the shim independently (semver) or tie it to runtime releases? I'd vote independent semver to avoid forcing partners to upgrade for unrelated runtime patches.
Daniel (product): Independent semver makes sense. We'll call out compatibility matrix in the doc.
Nina (partnerships): Great — thanks everyone. I'll post the draft doc shortly. If anyone has partner-specific constraints (signed-by vendor, notarization), ping me privately so I can capture them for the marketplace onboarding checklist.
Alex (partner-eng): pinged two partners who requested notarized macOS binaries historically — will add notes.
Sam (legal): Adding flag: "Customers choosing extended support must sign the addendum before shim removal."
Nina (partnerships): Logged. End of thread for now — will share doc link when ready.
